# GDT113 — page-conditioned record-code synthesis

## Leading theory

**PAGE_CONDITIONED_RECORD_CODE**

The strongest current generative theory is no longer “stable content-bearing
PAGE_HOST plus detachable renderer.” It is a page/register-conditioned codebook
whose codeword body and final edge are jointly generated inside a record
compiler. Any recoverable content association is now predicted to live first
at the **record/template and page-codebook level**, not at isolated exact hosts.

This theory scores 9/10 abductively versus compressed natural language 4/10,
stable token notation 5/10, and the prior hybrid content-address model 5/10.
The score is explanatory judgment, not statistical evidence.

## Why it leads

- PAGE_HOST is excellent internal page-local vocabulary but fails broad
  external transfer in GDT109 and GDT112.
- Final host character predicts renderer state manuscript-wide and predicts DY
  closure by +4,658.949 held bits in GDT111.
- The following host is harmful for DY prediction; the full transition is
  79.406 bits worse than previous-host trigrams alone. DY is edge licensing,

not a supported transition algebra.
- q-O early and d-Y late routing survives tails, folios and registers but is
  also a first-character string rule.
- GDT003's formal rectangles do not beat character/string statistics, exactly
  as a productive record-code generator predicts.
- External single-host glosses are unstable; B3 remains near-neutral and
  RIGHT_FAMILY remains register-conditioned rendering.

## Translation route

The next path is to align **whole repeated record templates** to independently
varying external structures, then infer which field substitutions track those
structures. Glossing PAGE_HOSTs first is now the wrong level. A successful
record-level alignment could later make codeword identities interpretable;
without that alignment, isolated host meanings will continue to overfit.

All ten hypothesis states, four compared theories, nine formal components,
five representative parses, and five new non-f84 predictions are exported.
No semantic assignments are made. f84r receives no prediction and remains
completely sealed: it was not opened, retained, queried, joined, scored, or
targeted.

# GDT113 — page-conditioned record-code synthesis

## Purpose

Revise the leading YOLO generative theory after GDT109–GDT112. This is abductive
model construction, not a confirmatory experiment. It binds the strongest
formal results and the new external-transfer failures into one explicit model
that can guide the next route toward content recovery.

## Compared theories

1. compressed/abbreviated natural language;
2. semantic/technical notation with stable token identities;
3. hybrid language plus abbreviation/notation with token-level content
   addresses;
4. page-conditioned record code: a page/register codebook plus a finite-state
   renderer, with any content association primarily above individual hosts.

The synthesis must choose one leader. It may use post-hoc explanatory fit, but
every supporting and awkward result is named. No archived semantic result is
treated as confirmation.

## Required revisions

- PAGE_HOST remains a useful formal codeword body but is no longer called a
  content address.
- The final PAGE_HOST character is a coupled edge state, not removable syntax.
- q and d remain strongly supported branch/placement routers.

- DY is licensed by the preceding host edge; GDT111 rejects a transferable
  pre→post PAGE_HOST transition algebra under the tested model.
- RIGHT_FAMILY remains register/host-conditioned rendering.
- O/OT remains a placement frame; broad external association is not preserved.
- B3 remains the best content-neutral closing control.

## Claim ceiling

The result is an explicit formal encoding theory and translation research
route. It does not establish that the manuscript is meaningful, nor assign a
semantic role, gloss, word, morpheme, POS, sound, language, plaintext, meaning,
or translation. f84r remains completely sealed and receives no prediction.

GDT113 adds a page/register-conditioned record-template prediction, but does not create a separate semantic candidate or justify a rerun of isolated-host work.
semantic_limit: The architecture comparison does not establish semantic readiness. GDT113 explicitly makes no semantic assignments; record/compiler structure and renderer prediction remain formal evidence.
changed_input_gate: A legitimate next test requires a frozen set of repeated record templates, an independently varying external structure with provenance-clean bindings, preregistered field substitutions, and held-record prediction showing content-linked variation beyond page/register and string/edge controls. A new host gloss, another abductive score, or isolated renderer success is insufficient.
